title: Index Pairs of a String
prompt:
Given a string `text` and an array of strings `words`, return an array of all index pairs `[i, j]` such that the substring `text[i..j]` (inclusive on both ends) equals some word in `words`.

Return the pairs sorted first by `i`, and if `i` is the same, then by `j`.

examples.explanation: "story" occurs at indices 3-7, "fleet" occurs at indices 9-13, "leetcode" occurs at indices 10-17.
"ab" occurs starting at index 0 and index 2. "aba" occurs starting at index 0 and index 2, both overlapping matches are included.

constraints: text and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters
All strings in words are distinct
hints: With such small constraints, checking every starting index against every word directly is already fast enough, but a trie lets you check all words sharing a prefix in one pass down from each starting index.

Insert all words into a trie. For each starting index i in text, walk down the trie following text's characters starting at i; whenever you land on a node marked as a word's end, record the pair [i, current index].
Continue the trie walk past a matched word's end (don't stop early) since a longer word in the dictionary might share the same prefix and also match starting at the same index.

solution.approach: Insert every word into a trie, marking word-ending nodes. For each starting index i in text, walk down the trie one character at a time following text[i], text[i+1], ... as far as the trie path exists; every time the current node is marked as a word ending, record the pair [i, current index] before continuing the walk (a longer dictionary word could share the same prefix, so we don't stop at the first match). This checks all words sharing prefixes together in a single walk per starting index rather than restarting a full string comparison per word.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n * maxWordLength) where n is the length of text
solution.spaceComplexity: O(sum of word lengths) for the trie
